The Sun satisfies both conditions: it’s extremely bright, emits the full spectrum, and its great distance makes its light rays nearly parallel when they hit a raindrop. Each droplet then refracts, reflects, and disperses those parallel rays at a fixed angle (≈42°), and many droplets together create the visible arc.

Hence we rarely see rainbows from artificial lights.
